methodology: The decomposition process involves breaking down the original research topic and the generated technical specification into atomic units. The criteria for each unit are independence, technical specificity, unambiguity, and implementability as a single requirement. The approach involves identifying key functionalities, behaviors, and constraints. For the original research topic, I extracted the core requirements directly from the text. For the generated specification, I analyzed the provided JSON structures and extracted the relevant information from the 'header', 'combinational_logic_function', 'enhanced_combinational_description', 'Interface Behavior', 'Timing Dependency', and 'Timing logic' sections. Each atomic unit represents a single, testable aspect of the design.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Shift data from input 'in' to output 'out'

spec_atomic_units: Module has clk, resetn, in, and out ports
clk is clock input
resetn is active-low synchronous reset input
in is data input
out is data output
Shift register shifts data on rising edge of clk
resetn resets register synchronously with clk
Combinational logic determines the next state
D flip-flop has D, CLK, and Q
Q at next clock cycle based on D at current cycle
resetn used to synchronously reset flip-flops
Shift register composed of four D flip-flops
Output of each flip-flop (except last) connected to input of next
in connected to input of first flip-flop
out is output of last flip-flop
resetn is connected to control input of multiplexers
Output 'out' is directly connected to the output of the last D flip-flop
D flip-flop stores value on D at rising edge of clk
Output Q reflects stored data
resetn asserted (low), outputs (Q) of all four flip-flops are set to 0
Combinational logic within each flip-flop can be described as a multiplexer controlled by the 'resetn' signal
Multiplexer selects between input data (D) and a reset value (0)
Data shifts from one flip-flop to the next at each clock cycle
Output 'out' reflects the value of the last flip-flop in the chain
The module has four input ports: clk, resetn, in, and out.
The clk is the clock signal, resetn is the active-low synchronous reset, in is the input data, and out is the output data.
The shift register shifts data on the rising edge of clk.
The resetn signal, when low, resets the register synchronously with the clock.
The data at the 'in' port is sampled on the rising edge of the 'clk' signal.
'resetn' signal must be stable before the rising edge of 'clk' to ensure proper reset operation.
The output 'out' reflects the shifted data, with a delay determined by the propagation delay of the flip-flops and any combinational logic.
The design uses four D flip-flops internally.
The 'always' block is triggered by the positive edge of 'clk'.
Inside the 'always' block, there is a conditional statement that checks the 'resetn' signal.
If 'resetn' is low, the register is reset to 0.
Otherwise, the data shifts from 'in' to the first flip-flop, and the outputs of the previous flip-flops are shifted to the next flip-flop.
The output 'out' is assigned the value of the last flip-flop.
The design uses non-blocking assignments (<=) to update the flip-flop values.
The internal registers are declared using the 'reg' keyword.
